summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, HIV, atrial fibrillation, and recent MRSA catheter infection was admitted for shortness of breath and fatigue after missing a dialysis session. She was volume overloaded with hyperkalemia and metabolic derangements, which improved with fluid management and two dialysis treatments. Her hypotension remained asymptomatic and was managed with increased midodrine. MRSA bacteremia treatment continued with vancomycin, and her fluconazole course for candidal esophagitis was completed. Warfarin was maintained for anticoagulation due to atrial fibrillation, IVC stenosis, and catheter thrombosis risk. She stabilized, labs improved, and she was discharged home with follow-up plans in primary care, dermatology, and allergy, along with continuation of all prescribed therapies.
